periods.analysis: K-12 Enrollment stands at 244000 students, which keeps Harborview in green and above the 240000 target. This is our starting quarter for this arc, so there is no quarter-over-quarter movement to report, but the fall count confirms that families are still choosing Harborview schools even as the region grows more expensive. The strongest intake came through the Airport North, Bayline, and East Harbor elementary feeders, while our Student Assignment Center cleared late registrations from new seaport logistics and airport service-worker families before the October close. I read this as healthy demand, not permission to relax, because enrollment strength depends on housing stability, reliable transportation, and safe school climates working together.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by extending the Welcome Harborview enrollment clinics at the airport workforce center, the Pier 6 family resource hub, and the East Harbor library through the next registration window. Ask Planning and Housing to give the district a monthly multifamily-permit feed by school attendance zone so we can staff classrooms ahead of the move-in curve. Keep bilingual enrollment navigators assigned to the Bayline and Airport North feeders, where same-week registration volume is highest.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 242200 students, down 1800 from 244000, but still green and still above the 240000 target. The movement is consistent with the winter pattern we see when families relocate after lease renewals and when older students enter midyear work-study or alternative programs. Our transfer desk saw the largest outflow from the Central Shore and West Flats zones, where rent pressure is changing household decisions faster than our annual boundary models can absorb. Even with the decline, campus principals kept class sections stable by using substitute-to-permanent conversion pools and targeted paraprofessional assignments rather than broad schedule disruption.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green position by keeping current staffing allocations through the spring count instead of reacting too quickly to a one-quarter dip. Extend exit-interview calls for every withdrawing family in Central Shore and West Flats, coding housing cost, transportation, safety, and program-fit reasons in the enrollment dashboard. Use those findings to shape the February magnet and career-pathway outreach, especially for students considering non-district options.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 240500 students, down 1700 from 242200, and remains green by a narrow 500-student margin over the 240000 target. The trend is now three quarters of softening, so I am treating the green status as earned but fragile. Kindergarten preregistration held up in the East Harbor and Southport corridors, while grades 9 and 10 showed more churn tied to family moves and credit-recovery placement. The Enrollment Services team used the HarborTrack student information system to reconcile duplicate records from charter returns and airport-area newcomers, which helped us keep the count clean rather than artificially inflated.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green by launching the spring Stay Enrolled campaign before families sign new leases, with school-based teams calling students flagged for address instability or repeated transportation requests. Extend the high-school reengagement cohort model at Harborview High, Seaport Tech, and Bayline Academy so ninth- and tenth-graders see a viable path inside the district. Prepare a contingency staffing plan for 239000 to 240000 enrollment, but do not implement reductions unless the next official count confirms the drop.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 238600 students, down 1900 from 240500, moving the measure to yellow because we are below the 240000 target while still above the 234000 red threshold. This is the first quarter where the trend is no longer just watchful background noise; it has crossed into operational risk for classroom planning, transportation routing, and school-budget assumptions. The largest pressure points are in the coastal apartment belts from Tidegate to West Flats, where families are reporting rent increases, doubled-up housing, and longer commutes after moves inland. At the same time, new seats in the North Harbor development have not yet translated into enrolled students because building certificates and family occupancy are lagging the school calendar.
periods.recommendations: Move from monitoring to intervention by creating a yellow-status enrollment command review every two weeks with Student Assignment, Transportation, Housing, and Planning at the table. Set a watch-item on the Tidegate, West Flats, and Central Shore feeders, with principals reporting weekly withdrawals, no-shows, and midyear return inquiries. Extend mobile registration to the North Harbor and Southport permit corridors so families can enroll as soon as leases and certificates of occupancy are issued.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 236667 students, down 1933 from 238600, keeping the measure yellow and confirming that the decline has not yet bottomed out. We opened the year with strong front-office execution, but fewer students walked through the doors than our spring projection assumed, especially in middle grades where families are most likely to move for housing and childcare reasons. The Welcome Week verification teams cleared backlogs at 41 campuses, and the district added temporary route checks on the 12, 47, and HarborLink school corridors to see whether transportation friction was contributing to non-enrollment. My concern is not the accuracy of the count; it is the persistence of the pattern.
periods.recommendations: Keep the yellow response active and assign an enrollment recovery target by feeder pattern rather than one citywide number, starting with Bayline, Central Shore, and Tidegate. Continue the transportation watch-item by comparing withdrawal addresses with missed-stop data from the first 30 school days, then adjust routes where a modest change can keep students connected. Expand the newcomer and returner enrollment clinics into evening hours during October, staffed by bilingual registrars and McKinney-Vento liaisons.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 235000 students, down 1667 from 236667, still yellow and now only 1000 students above the red threshold of 234000. The quarter-over-quarter loss slowed somewhat, which tells me the interventions may be reducing the slope, but the district has not stabilized the base. Chronic absenteeism and housing instability are now intersecting with enrollment risk, particularly for students in temporary shelter or doubled-up arrangements near the downtown and port-adjacent corridors. Principals used the HarborStay roster review to identify students who were absent before formal withdrawal, and that gave outreach teams a better chance to keep families connected before records were requested elsewhere.
periods.recommendations: Treat 234000 as the hard watch-line and require weekly review of feeders projected to fall below plan in January. Extend HarborStay into a joint attendance-and-enrollment protocol, so a student with repeated absences, an address change, and a transportation complaint receives one coordinated family contact rather than three separate calls. Hold spring staffing decisions at the school level until the January reconciliation is complete, using central vacancy control instead of classroom-level disruption where possible.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 233200 students, down 1800 from 235000, which moves the measure to red because it is below the 234000 threshold. I am concerned, and I want to be clear about that, but the situation is being actively managed with better data and tighter field response than we had a year ago. The deepest losses are in grades 6 through 10 across the West Flats, Central Shore, and Bayline feeders, where families cite housing cost, shelter transitions, and long cross-town commutes after relocation. The red status means enrollment decline is now a system-level risk to course access, transportation efficiency, and student belonging, not simply a budgeting issue.
periods.recommendations: Activate the red-status Enrollment Stabilization Plan for the affected feeders, with named owners for family outreach, transportation fixes, shelter coordination, and high-school reentry. Deploy central registrars to West Flats Community School, Bayline Academy, and the downtown family navigation center three days per week until the next count. Protect core academic offerings by pooling low-enrollment electives across nearby high schools and using virtual sections only where they preserve, rather than replace, student access.

periods.analysis: Enrollment is 231500 students, down 1700 from 233200, remaining red and extending the eight-quarter decline from the 244000 baseline. The loss is slightly smaller than last quarter, but red is red, and 231500 students puts us 8500 below the 240000 target. We are seeing some promising returns from shelter-based registration and airport-employer family outreach, yet they are not enough to offset withdrawals tied to housing affordability and moves beyond district boundaries. The operational work is now focused on preserving stable school communities while rebuilding the intake pipeline for the next school year.
periods.recommendations: Continue the red-status Enrollment Stabilization Plan through summer and set feeder-level recovery goals before budget adoption, not after school opens. Expand partnerships with Housing, the Continuum of Care, and major airport and port employers so families receive school enrollment support at the same time they receive housing or workforce assistance. For the next quarter, require a public dashboard that separates new enrollments, verified withdrawals, no-shows, and returns, so the Board and principals can see which lever is actually moving.

periods.analysis: Enrollment fell from 231,500 to 230,900 students, leaving a 9,100-student gap to the 240,000 target. Registration outreach has not yet offset withdrawals and family mobility.
periods.recommendations: Review feeder-level new registrations, verified withdrawals, no-shows and returns separately so the next enrollment response addresses the source of the decline.
